chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about a slave who falsely accuses a free man. He said: "He is flogged as a hadd punishment."

key_terms.حَدًّا: as a hadd punishment; a fixed legal penalty
key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: falsely accuses or fabricates a charge against someone
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is flogged; the prescribed corporal punishment is carried out
key_terms.ٱلْحُرِّ: a free man; the person against whom the false accusation is made
key_terms.ٱلْعَبْدِ: a slave; the legally subordinate person mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave falsely accuses a free man in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave who makes a false accusation against a free person. It establishes that the offender is subject to hadd punishment, reflecting the seriousness of false accusation in Islamic law.
